subject: Architecture
title: The Lotus Temple: Bahá'í House of Worship
description: A quick win: understand The Lotus Temple: Bahá'í House of Worship.

hook.text: Delhi's Lotus Temple is shaped like a giant lotus flower with 27 marble petals — and it welcomes every religion.

buildup.text: Built in 1986, the Bahá'í temple has no religious images, statues, or symbols inside — only silence.

discovery.text: The nine-sided design represents the Bahá'í principle of unity — the highest single digit, symbolizing completeness.

twist.text: It receives more visitors than the Taj Mahal — over 100 million since it opened, from every faith and none.

climax.text: The petals are self-cleaning white concrete. Natural ventilation cools the interior without air conditioning.

punchline.text: A temple for everyone. More popular than a monument to love.

quiz.question: How does the Lotus Temple compare to the Taj Mahal in visitors?
options: It receives about the same number annually
It receives more visitors overall since opening
The Taj Mahal receives significantly more visitors

details.summary: The Lotus Temple in New Delhi (1986) is a Bahá'í House of Worship shaped like a half-open lotus flower with 27 freestanding marble-clad petals. It welcomes worshippers of all religions and none, receiving over 4 million visitors annually — more than the Taj Mahal.
details.whyItMatters: The Lotus Temple proves that sacred architecture doesn't require historical references. A completely novel form — a concrete flower — creates sacred space as effectively as any Gothic cathedral.
takeaways: 27 marble-clad petals form a half-open lotus flower shape
Welcomes all faiths, receiving 4+ million visitors annually
Novel form proves sacred space doesn't require traditional styles

faq.question: Why was the lotus shape chosen?
faq.answer: The lotus is sacred across Hinduism, Buddhism, and other Asian traditions — it grows from mud to bloom in purity, symbolizing spiritual emergence. For the Bahá'í faith, it represents purity and unity.

faq.question: How was the complex curved structure built?
faq.answer: The 27 petals are reinforced concrete shells clad in white Greek marble. Each petal has a unique geometry requiring specialized formwork. Canadian architect Fariborz Sahba worked with structural engineer Flint and Neill to translate the organic form into buildable concrete sections.
